requirement:
When source-access policy denies a mandatory input, the assessment MUST abort
before any model request and report the denied path and reason to its caller;
for an untracked file, the report MUST say what {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial.untracked`
says. The aborted assessment MUST NOT write evidence or emit evidence JSON, and
its usage record MUST identify the failure. In a batch, other assessments MUST
continue, including queued assessments, and their successful writes MUST be
retained; the command MUST return a nonzero exit status after the batch
finishes.
rationale:
The requirement is satisfied.

| Obligation | Implementation and verification |
|---|---|
| Abort a denied assessment before any model request. | `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[configured_record]` calls `AuthoringSubject::sources` with `?` before connecting to either provider path. `src/authoring/inputs.rs#impl[AssessmentSources]/fn[prepare]` propagates access failures, including anchor failures. `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[a_denied_mandatory_input_aborts_only_its_assessment]` asserts no request for the denied subject and a zero request count; `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[unreadable_or_denied_anchors_fail_before_inference]` also checks preparation failure. |
| Report the denied path to the caller. | Preparation preserves access errors and adds anchor context; `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[author_evidence_with_options]` and `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[prepare_assessment]` propagate them. Both integration tests assert the denied path in diagnostics. |
| Report the denial reason to the caller. | `src/authoring/access.rs#impl[SourceAccess]/fn[path]`, reached through `SourceAccess::file`, returns descriptive denial errors; those errors survive propagation. `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[an_untracked_mandatory_input_is_reported_with_how_to_stage_it]` asserts the untracked reason in the caller's diagnostic. |
| For untracked inputs, apply `requirements.authoring.read_denial.untracked`'s reporting rule. | The same `SourceAccess::path` error identifies the file as untracked and explains `git add` and a workspace allow rule. The untracked integration test exercises mandatory-input preparation and asserts all these diagnostic components. This checks application of the cited requirement, not its independent implementation. |
| Do not write evidence for the aborted assessment. | `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[configured_assessment]` writes only after successful `configured_record`; batch staging likewise occurs only for successful preparation in `src/authoring/batch.rs#fn[run_batch]`. The denied-input integration test asserts no evidence file. |
| Do not emit evidence JSON for the aborted assessment. | `configured_assessment` reaches stdout serialization only after successful preparation. The denied-input integration test separately invokes `--stdout` and asserts empty stdout. |
| Identify failure in the usage record. | Both `author_evidence_with_options` and `prepare_assessment` finish denial errors as `failed`; `src/authoring/usage.rs#impl[UsageLog]/fn[finish]` records and saves that outcome. The denied-input integration test asserts `failed`, zero requests, and `evidence_written: false`. |
| Continue other batch assessments. | `run_batch` records individual failures and continues its loop. `src/authoring/batch.rs#fn[cancel_on_error]` cancels only on interruption, not access denial. The denied-input integration test verifies successful evidence from the other subjects. |
| Continue queued assessments. | The same loop continues launching work after denial. The integration test uses concurrency one specifically so subsequent successful assessments were queued. |
| Retain successful writes. | Successful results proceed through `src/authoring/batch.rs#fn[stage_record]` and `src/authoring/batch.rs#fn[persist_record]`; a denial neither cancels these commits nor rolls them back. The integration test reads and verifies the other subjects' retained evidence. |
| Return a nonzero command status after the batch finishes. | `src/main.rs#fn[main]` awaits the batch, then returns an error if its collected failures are nonempty. The integration test asserts unsuccessful command status while also verifying the completed queued assessments' evidence. |

The implementation is reachable from the subject's marked roots, and the cited integration tests carry the subject's `{test}` reference. No unacknowledged gap was found.
